items.concept: Bandaged infirmary nurse: wet head-wrap, no face, neck bent wrong, dragging a rusted bone saw.
items.flavor: She still does rounds. You are the round. The bandages are not for her face. They are for yours, after.

items.concept: Net-sack fisherman: a sailcloth sack on two bare legs, split open at the chest with rope and fish hooks spilling out.
items.flavor: Somebody sewed him shut so the sea would not want him. The sea did not want him. Neither do you. Keep walking.

items.concept: Faceless dockworker: flat cap over a smooth membrane where a face should be, backward knees, fog leaking from his coat. (He came back holding a lantern; that can be taken out.)
items.flavor: He punched in at six. He never punched out. His face stopped bothering to be one. Fog is what a man breathes out when he forgets.

items.concept: The Harbourmaster: a heavy brass-buttoned officer, his right shoulder burst into raw tissue with one yellow eye and an overgrown arm. Still human-faced. (He also carries a lantern.)
items.flavor: Every ship that leaves, he logs. Nothing leaves. The eye on his shoulder keeps the books now. It never blinks. Neither will you.

items.concept: The Lighthouse Keeper: oilskin and sou'wester, an eye bulging from his neck, his left arm split into a dragging limb studded with eyes and ending in a claw. He carries a lamp.
items.flavor: He kept the light on for forty years. Then the light started keeping him. Count the eyes on the arm. Now count them again. There's one more.

items.concept: The Surgeon: a smiling top-hatted doctor with spectacles, his apron split over a huge slit-pupil eye in his chest; doctor's bag and amputation knife.
items.flavor: He washes his hands between patients. Out of habit. Out of courtesy. This won't hurt, he says. He is a doctor. Doctors lie.

items.concept: The Raven-thing: a mourning frock coat on a man's frame, a matted raven head with one milky eye, talons and bird legs, paper scraps in its feathers.
items.flavor: You ask it how many nights are left. It tells you. It always tells you the same number. The number is the one you were afraid of.

items.concept: The Tell-Tale: a nightcapped old man built from floorboards and nails, one huge filmy blue vulture eye, a beating red heart in his rib-cage, dragging a crowbar.
items.flavor: You hear it before you see it. Under the boards. Under your boots. Under your own ribs. Louder. It isn't his heart anymore. It's yours, keeping time.

items.concept: The Red Death: a tall shrouded reveller in a cracked porcelain mask weeping blood, with a stopped clock pendant. (Generated without the anchor as a test; no lantern crept in.)
items.flavor: The party is still going. The clock stopped at midnight and nobody noticed. You noticed. That's how it knows you're a guest.
